actual.value:
Despite the aforementioned three negative external factors in the project environment, the partners managed to implement the project according to plans. All initially set key objectives have been met. In summary, the following achievements are worth mentionning:
1) At the level of the four organisations
- 20 super-trainers and 15 local participants trained on various SRHR themes (training sessions held consecutively in Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, Benin) in the ranks of staff from the four beneficiary organizations (ADEP, SONGES, AfriYAN, UP)
- 02 television films on virtual reality produced on the dangers linked to the abuse of the consumption of psychotropic products and menstrual hygiene.
- establishment of a sub-regional network for the promotion of SRHR for the benefit of adolescents and young people.
2) At the level of the targets groups: the school communities
- Benin: 12 trainers, 24 young leaders trained, 6317 pupils sensitized in the schools
-Burkina Faso: 10 trainers, 61 young leaders trained (i.e. 31 girls and 30 boys),and 741 pupils sensitized in the schools.
-Niger: 15 trainers, 25 young leaders trained, 1327 students educated (i.e. 755 girls and 572 boys)
-Mali: 15 trainers

I. (Phase 1: April 1 - December 31, 2021): **capacity building for “super trainers”** The 1st phase of the project consisted of capacity building for the “super trainers” of the four beneficiary organizations. In total, five (05) training sessions for “super trainers” were organized as part of the 1st phase of this TMT+. It was about: • April 19-25, 2021 in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso: 1st training session for “super-trainers”: SRHR and in particular AYSRH, Communication for Social and Behavioral Change (CCSC) and the guiding principles for the promotion of Complete Sexuality Education (CSE). This 1st training workshop was organized on the sidelines of the official launching ceremony of the project which saw the effective participation of the Ambassador of the Netherlands in Burkina Faso. This first TMT+ activity was organized in two consecutive stages and covered a total of five (5) days. Its implementation was carried out as follows: - the first part (0.5 days) consisted of the actual holding of the launch ceremony with the participation of stakeholders; - the second part (4.5 days) was used for the actual training. • May 16-23, 2021 in Bamako, Mali: 2nd training session for “super-trainers”: Health services adapted to the needs of adolescents and young people • 13-20 June in Niamey, Niger: 3rd training session for “super-trainers”: Community participation and ownership and quick-win advocacy in SRHR • August 9-15, 2021 in Parakou, Benin: 4th training session for “super-trainers”: Knowledge and practices of Gender & Governance markers, Change-Oriented Approaches (AOC) and Monitoring • September 26-October 1, 2021 in Cotonou, Benin: 5th training session for “super-trainers”: training/action workshop for actors & production of a pilot VR video N.B.: August 30-November 4, 2021 was the operationalization period for this VR activity. The VR work was spread over a period of two consecutive months during which actions were carried out in three interdependent and complementary stages. Most of this work was done remotely (online). The Cotonou workshop marked the face-to-face stage of the work. This process of capacity building for "super trainers" was intended to enable these four direct beneficiary organizations ADEP, SONGES, AfriYAN and UP to acquire the necessary capacities in SDSR and in communication on sexuality enabling them to effectively promote sexual and reproductive health and rights in schools. Thus, at the end of this 1st phase of the project, these organizations saw their capacities reinforced. ADEP, SONGES, AfriYAN and UP have thus become capable of adequately training and raising awareness among key players in education (teachers, parents, peer educators, students) and also stakeholders in the school environment (opinion leaders , communities, sectoral ministries of health and education, private sector of health or education, associations especially those of young people, NGOs, etc.) to alleviate the multiple concerns in this area of SRHR in establishments primary, secondary and university education. In total, 20 "super trainers" at the rate of a core of 5 per organization have benefited from the complete training course. They thus participated in the various training workshops which took place on a rolling basis in the 4 countries involved. It should be noted that these "super trainers" appointed by the organizations included individuals with the following profiles: head of NGO/Structure; programme/project manager / Planners / supervisor responsible for field operations; trainer with skills in community training or animation; youth (vibrant 20-24 year old woman belonging to an official country-wide representative youth association – activist, blogger, slammer, etc.) with skills in community animation.
To these 20 "super trainers" were added 15 trainers who benefited from the training on only some of the topics covered.
II. (Phase 2: January 1 - March 31, 2022): **Piloting for the benefit of targets in establishments** This 2nd phase of the project comes after the 1st phase of the project which consisted of capacity building for the “super trainers” of the four beneficiary organizations. During this 2nd phase, these four beneficiary organizations (ADEP, AfriYAN, SONGES, UP) take advantage of the achievements they have made during the 1st phase of the project for the benefit of targets in selected pilot schools. This piloting process for the benefit of the targets in the chosen establishments is an opportunity for the “super trainers” trained to put into practice the knowledge acquired during their own training. It is therefore an opportunity for these "super trainers" to put into practice the knowledge gained from the training course they have benefited from. Steering for the benefit of targets has three (03) major components: 1. Training of trainers (teachers, heads of establishments, representatives of ministries, parents of students, etc.) 2. Training of Youth Leaders/peer educators (pupils, students) 3. Training and awareness campaigns for school and university communities During the period indicated, various activities were carried out and results achieved. Thus, in each of the four countries, the organizations carried out the following preparatory activities:  A workshop for the appropriation and preparation of the contents of the SRHR modules according to the context of the country. This workshop was organized internally by each of the organizations.  Finalization of the list of establishments: each organization has taken the appropriate steps with the state authorities at the national and decentralized level for the designation of the pilot establishments which will directly benefit from the piloting  Identification of teachers: the lists of trainers to be trained have thus been established  Monitoring of student identification by teachers: lists of Youth Leaders/peer educators have been established These preparatory activities made it possible to begin the operationalization of the 3 major components of management. The following overall results have already been achieved: • Training of trainers: in total, 67 trainers selected in 31 pilot establishments targeted in the four countries combined, were trained by the "super trainers" of ADEP, AfriYAN, SONGES and UP, with a view to creating a critical mass of teachers to oversee the promotion of SRHR within their respective establishments. These training sessions led by the “super trainers” took place under the supervision of experts from the consortium. • Training of Youth Leaders: with the exception of Mali, which has not yet been able to start for security reasons, the training workshops for peer educators have already started. Thus, more than 125 Youth Leaders have already been trained. • Training and awareness campaigns: in Burkina and Niger, which are already at this stage of operationalization, more than 500 students have already been reached. These numbers will increase in the coming weeks. N.B.: it should be noted that due to financial constraints, a reduction in the number of schools to be involved in the pilot has been made: of the 10 pilot schools initially planned, it has been agreed that each organization may be limited to 3 pilot schools at least in each country. This adjustment was the subject of a request submitted to the lessor Nuffic in mid-March 2022.
